complete_source_units.text: “When you measure out the land as an inheritance, you will set apart a first portion for the Lord, a holy part of the land, twenty-five thousand long and twenty thousand broad. It will be holy throughout all its boundaries all around.
From this, a square of five hundred by five hundred will be for a sanctuary, with an interval of fifty cubits all around it.
From this measured area you will measure a length of twenty-five thousand and a breadth of ten thousand. In it will be the sanctuary, the most holy place.
It will be land for the priests who minister in the holy place, for those who draw near to minister to the Lord. It will be a place for their houses, set apart for their sanctification.
An area twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand broad will belong to the Levites who minister to the house, as their possession, with cities in which to dwell.
You will give the city a possession five thousand broad and twenty-five thousand long; like the first portion of the holy areas, these will be for the whole house of Israel.

The ruler will have land on this side and that side of the first portions of the holy areas and the city’s possession, facing the first portions of the holy areas and facing the city’s possession: the parts toward the sea, and from those toward the sea toward the east. Its length will be like one of the portions, from the sea-facing boundaries, with the length extending to the eastern boundaries of the land.
It will be his possession in Israel. Israel’s rulers will no longer oppress My people, and the house of Israel will inherit the land according to their tribes.
Thus says the Lord God: Enough, rulers of Israel! Remove injustice and suffering, and practice judgment and righteousness. Take oppression away from My people, says the Lord God.
You are to have an honest balance, an honest measure, and an honest choenix.
The measure and the choenix will likewise have one capacity: the choenix a tenth of the gomor, and the measure a tenth of the gomor. They will be equal in relation to the gomor.
The standard weight will be twenty obols. The five shekels will be five, the ten shekels ten, and fifty shekels will make your mina.
This is the first portion you will set apart: a sixth of the measure from the gomor of wheat, and a sixth of the oiphi from the kor of barley.
The command for oil is a cotyle of oil from ten cotyles, because ten cotyles are a gomor.
One sheep from every ten sheep will be a contribution from all Israel’s families, for sacrifices, burnt offerings, and offerings for well-being, to make atonement for you, says the Lord God.
All the people will give this first portion to Israel’s ruler.

Through the ruler will come the burnt offerings, sacrifices, and libations at the festivals, new moons, and Sabbaths, and at all the festivals of the house of Israel. He will provide the offerings for sin, the sacrifice, the burnt offerings, and the offerings for well-being to make atonement for the house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord God: In the first month, on the first of the month, you all will take an unblemished calf from the cattle to make atonement for the holy place.

The priest will take some of the blood of the atonement offering and put it on the house’s doorposts, on the four corners of the sacred precinct, on the altar, and on the doorposts of the gate of the inner court.
You will do likewise in the seventh month, on the first of the month: you will take a portion from each, and you all will make atonement for the house.
In the first month, on the fourteenth of the month, you will have the Passover festival; for seven days you will eat unleavened bread.
On that day the ruler will provide a calf for sin on behalf of himself, the house, and all the people of the land.
For the seven days of the festival, he will provide burnt offerings to the Lord: seven calves and seven unblemished rams each day for the seven days, and a goat kid each day for sin.
You will provide an offering of a cake for each calf and a cake for each ram, with a hin of oil for each cake.
In the seventh month, on the fifteenth of the month, at the festival you will provide the same for seven days: the offerings for sin, the burnt offerings, the grain offering, and the oil.”
“Thus says the Lord God: The gate in the inner court facing east will be shut during the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it will be opened, and on the day of the new moon it will be opened.

The ruler will enter by the porch of the outer gate and stand at the gate’s vestibules. The priests will offer his burnt offerings and his offerings for well-being. He will bow down at the gate’s vestibule and go out, and the gate will certainly not be shut until evening.
The people of the land will bow down before the Lord at the vestibules of that gate on Sabbaths and new moons.
The ruler will present burnt offerings to the Lord: on the Sabbath day, six unblemished lambs and an unblemished ram,
with a grain offering of a cake for the ram, and for the lambs an offering as the gift of his hand, with a hin of oil for each cake.
On the day of the new moon there will be an unblemished calf and six lambs, and the ram will be unblemished.
A cake for the ram and a cake for the calf will be the grain offering, and for the lambs whatever his hand can produce, with a hin of oil for each cake.
When the ruler enters, he will enter by the porch of the gate and go out by the way of the gate.

When the people of the land come before the Lord at the festivals, whoever enters by the north gate to bow down will go out by the south gate, and whoever enters by the south gate will go out by the north gate. He will not return through the gate by which he entered, but will go out straight opposite it.
The ruler will be among them: when they enter, he will enter with them, and when they go out, he will go out.
At the festivals and public assemblies the grain offering will be a cake for each calf, a cake for each ram, and for the lambs whatever his hand can produce, with a hin of oil for each cake.

If the ruler makes a pledged offering, a burnt offering for well-being to the Lord, he will open for himself the gate facing east and offer his burnt offering and his offerings for well-being as he does on the Sabbath day. He will go out and close the doors after he has gone out.
He will prepare an unblemished year-old lamb as a daily burnt offering to the Lord; in the morning he will prepare it.
In the morning he will prepare with it a grain offering of a sixth of the measure and a third of a hin of oil to mix the fine flour: a grain offering to the Lord, a permanent command.
You all will prepare the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil; you all will prepare them in the morning as a continual burnt offering.
Thus says the Lord God: If the ruler gives one of his sons a gift from his inheritance, this will belong to his sons as an inherited possession.
If he gives a gift to one of his servants, it will belong to him until the year of release, and he will return it to the ruler. But the inheritance of his sons will belong to them.

The ruler will certainly not take from the people’s inheritance to oppress them. He will give his sons an inheritance from his own possession, so that none of My people is scattered from his possession.”
He brought me into the entrance behind the gate, into the north-facing recessed chamber of the priests’ holy places. Look—there was a separated place there.

He said to me, “This is the place where the priests will boil the offerings for ignorance and for sin, and there bake the entire grain offering, so as not to carry it out into the outer court and sanctify the people.”
He brought me out into the outer court and led me around its four sides. Look—a court at one side of the court, and a court at another side of the court!
At the four sides of the court was a small court, forty cubits long and thirty cubits broad; the four had one measure.
There were recessed chambers all around them, around the four, with kitchens made underneath the recessed chambers all around.
He said to me, “These are the kitchen houses, where those ministering to the house will boil the people’s sacrificial animals.”

He brought me to the house’s vestibules, and look—water was flowing out beneath the open court toward the east, for the house’s front faced east. The water was descending from the right side, from the south toward the altar.
He brought me out by the north gate and led me around outside to the court’s gate facing east. Look—the water was flowing down from the right side.
As the man went out opposite, with a measure in his hand, he measured a thousand with the measure and went through the water—water of release.
He measured a thousand and went through water up to the thighs. He measured a thousand and went through water up to the waist.
He measured a thousand and could not go through, for the water surged violently like the rush of a torrent that they will not cross.
He said to me, “Have you seen, son of man?” Then he led me to the river’s edge.
As I returned, look—very many trees were on the river’s edge, on both sides.
He said to me, “This water flowing out into eastern Galilee was descending into Arabia and coming as far as the sea, to the water of the outlet; it will heal the waters.

Every life among the swarming living creatures will live wherever the river comes. There will be very many fish there, because this water has arrived there, and it will become healthy and live. Everything over which the river comes will live.
Fishers will stand there from Aingadin to Ainagalim; there will be a drying place for nets. It will be by itself, and its fish will be like the fish of the Great Sea, an exceedingly great multitude.
At its outlet, at its turning, and at its overflow, they will certainly not be healed; they are given over to salt.

Along the river, on its edge on both sides, every edible tree will grow. Nothing upon it will grow old, nor will its fruit fail. In its newness it will bear its first crop, because these waters flow from the holy places. Their fruit will be for food and their growth for health.
Thus says the Lord God: These are the boundaries of the land you will allot as an inheritance to the twelve tribes of the sons of Israel—an addition of a measured portion.
You will inherit it, each like his brother, the land for which I raised My hand to give it to their fathers. This land will fall to you as an inheritance.
These are the boundaries of the land toward the north: from the Great Sea, descending and dividing at the entrance of Hamath—Seddada,
Berotha, Sebraim, Heliam, between the boundaries of Damascus and the boundaries of Hamath, the court of Saunan, which are above the boundaries of Auranitis.
These are the boundaries from the sea, from the court of Ainan, the boundaries of Damascus, and the parts toward the north.
The eastern parts lie between Auranitis and Damascus, and between Galaaditis and the land of Israel; the Jordan marks the boundary as far as the sea east of Palm Grove. These are the eastern parts.
The parts toward the south and southwest run from Thaiman and Palm Grove to the water of Marimoth Kades, extending to the Great Sea. This is the south and southwest side.
This is the side of the Great Sea: it forms the boundary as far as opposite the entrance of Hamath, as far as its entrance. These are the sea-facing parts of Hamath.
You will divide this land for them, for the tribes of Israel.

You will cast lots for it for yourselves and for the sojourners dwelling among you who have fathered sons among you. They will be to you as native-born among the sons of Israel; with you they will eat from an inheritance among Israel’s tribes.
They will be in a tribe of sojourners, among the sojourners who are with them; there you will give them an inheritance, says the Lord God.

These are the names of the tribes: from the northern beginning, along the side of the descending, dividing way toward the entrance of Hamath, the court of Ainan, the boundary of Damascus toward the north, along the side of Hamath’s court; the eastern parts as far as the sea will belong to them—Dan, one portion.
From Dan’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Asher, one portion.
From Asher’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Naphtali, one portion.
From Naphtali’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Manasseh, one portion.
From Manasseh’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Ephraim, one portion.
From Ephraim’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Reuben, one portion.
From Reuben’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Judah, one portion.

From Judah’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts, will be the first portion set apart, twenty-five thousand in breadth, with a length like one of the portions from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts. The holy place will be in their midst.
The first portion they set apart for the Lord will be twenty-five thousand long and twenty-five thousand broad.

From these will be the first portion of the holy areas for the priests: twenty-five thousand toward the north, a breadth of ten thousand toward the sea, a breadth of ten thousand toward the east, and a length of twenty-five thousand toward the south. The mountain of the holy places will be in its midst,
for the consecrated priests, the sons of Zadok, who keep the duties of the house and did not stray when the sons of Israel strayed, as the Levites strayed.
They will have the first portion given from the land’s first portions, most holy, from the Levites’ boundaries.
The Levites will have the land adjoining the priests’ boundaries, twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand broad. The whole length will be twenty-five thousand and the breadth twenty thousand.
None of it will be sold or measured out, nor will the land’s first produce be taken away, for it is holy to the Lord.
The five thousand remaining in breadth alongside the twenty-five thousand will be a forewall for the city, for dwelling and its intervening space. The city will be in its midst.

These are its measurements: on the north, four thousand five hundred; on the south, four thousand five hundred; on the east, four thousand five hundred; and toward the sea, four thousand five hundred.
The city will have an intervening space: two hundred fifty toward the north, two hundred fifty toward the south, two hundred fifty toward the east, and two hundred fifty toward the sea.

The remaining length adjoining the first portions of the holy areas will be ten thousand toward the east and ten thousand toward the sea; these will be the holy place’s first portions, and its produce will be bread for the city’s workers.
The city’s workers, from all Israel’s tribes, will work it.
The entire first portion will be twenty-five thousand by twenty-five thousand. You will set apart its holy portion as a square, from the city’s possession.

The remainder will belong to the ruler on this side and that side, from the holy first portions and toward the city’s possession, extending twenty-five thousand in length to the eastern boundaries, and toward the sea extending twenty-five thousand to the sea-facing boundaries, adjoining the ruler’s portions. The first portion of the holy areas and the house’s sanctuary will be in its midst.
From the Levites’ possession and from the city’s possession, it will be in the midst of the rulers; between Judah’s boundaries and Benjamin’s boundaries it will belong to the rulers.
As for the remaining tribes, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Benjamin, one portion.
From Benjamin’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Simeon, one portion.
From Simeon’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Issachar, one portion.
From Issachar’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Zebulun, one portion.
From Zebulun’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Gad, one portion.
From Gad’s boundaries toward the southwest, its boundaries will run from Thaiman and the water of Marimoth Kades, an inheritance as far as the Great Sea.
This is the land you will cast lots for among Israel’s tribes, and these are their divisions, says the Lord God.
These are the city’s outlets toward the north: four thousand five hundred by measure.
The city’s gates will bear the names of Israel’s tribes. Three gates will face north: one gate of Reuben, one gate of Judah, and one gate of Levi.
Toward the east, four thousand five hundred, with three gates: one gate of Joseph, one gate of Benjamin, and one gate of Dan.
Toward the south, four thousand five hundred by measure, with three gates: one gate of Simeon, one gate of Issachar, and one gate of Zebulun.
Toward the sea, four thousand five hundred by measure, with three gates: one gate of Gad, one gate of Asher, and one gate of Naphtali.
The circuit will be eighteen thousand. And the city’s name, from whatever day it comes into being, will be its name.”
